title: 计算机科学，从零搭建 · 第25部分：不可判定

chapters.Frontier: 15. 前沿：其他环上的希尔伯特第十问题
chapters.Outro: 回顾、习题，以及它们会在哪里再出现

8b09cc8965db.en: Here are three questions from three different worlds. <bookmark mark='a'/> First, geometry. Here are eleven square tiles with coloured edges. Can copies of them cover the whole plane, with touching edges always the same colour? <bookmark mark='b'/> A computer search finds a twelve-by-twelve patch at once, and larger ones too. But it never finds a pattern that repeats, and that is no accident. <bookmark mark='c'/> Second, number theory. Are there whole numbers x and y with x squared minus sixty-one y squared equal to one? Fermat posed this one as a challenge in 1657. <bookmark mark='d'/> Trying every y up to seventy-eight million found nothing in twenty seconds. The smallest answer has x near one point eight billion. <bookmark mark='e'/> Third, programs. Can a program print its own source code, exactly, without reading itself from a file? <bookmark mark='f'/> Yes: here is one in Python, and we wrote one in the Pebble language and ran it. <bookmark mark='g'/> This part is about the surprise that ties them together. Each of these questions is one case of a general problem that no algorithm can solve, and the reason, every time, is the halting problem of Part 1.
8b09cc8965db.zh: 这里有来自三个不同世界的三个问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一个，几何。这里有十一块边缘涂色的正方形砖。用它们的复制品能铺满整个平面，并且相接的边颜色总相同吗？<bookmark mark='b'/>计算机搜索立刻就能找到一块十二乘十二的拼片，更大的也行。但它从来找不到一个重复的图案，而这不是偶然。<bookmark mark='c'/>第二个，数论。有没有整数 x 和 y，使得 x 的平方减去六十一倍 y 的平方等于一？费马在1657年把它当作挑战提了出来。<bookmark mark='d'/>把 y 一直试到七千八百万，二十秒里一无所获。最小的解里，x 接近十八亿。<bookmark mark='e'/>第三个，程序。一个程序能不读取自己的文件，就精确地打印出自己的源代码吗？<bookmark mark='f'/>能：这里有一个 Python 的，我们还用 Pebble 语言写了一个并运行了它。<bookmark mark='g'/>这一部分讲的是把它们连在一起的那个意外。这些问题中的每一个，都是某个没有算法能解决的一般问题的特例，而原因每一次都是第1部分的停机问题。

b591563e63a2.en: Part 25 of Computer Science, Built: Undecidable. Act Five begins: limits and secrets. <bookmark mark='a'/> In this part: which problems can be decided, which can only be recognized, and how to carry undecidability from one problem to another; Rice's theorem, which forbids almost every question about what programs do; programs that print themselves; dominoes, tiles and Diophantine equations, each hiding a Turing machine; Gödel's incompleteness theorem, proved from the halting problem; oracles; Kolmogorov complexity and Chaitin's Omega; and the busy beavers once more, where provability itself runs out.
b591563e63a2.zh: 计算机科学，从零搭建，第25部分：不可判定。第五幕开始：极限与秘密。<bookmark mark='a'/>这一部分包括：哪些问题可以判定，哪些只能识别，以及如何把不可判定性从一个问题搬到另一个问题；Rice 定理，它禁止了几乎所有关于程序行为的问题；打印自身的程序；多米诺、砖块和丢番图方程，每一个里面都藏着一台图灵机；从停机问题证明的 Gödel 不完备定理；谕示；Kolmogorov 复杂度与 Chaitin 的 Omega；以及再一次的忙碌海狸，在那里可证明性本身也走到了尽头。

72c92f965265.en: Part 1 proved that the halting problem cannot be decided. This part makes the picture precise. <bookmark mark='a'/> A language is decidable if some machine always halts and answers correctly, yes or no. <bookmark mark='b'/> It is recognizable, or recursively enumerable, if some machine halts with yes on every member, but on the others is allowed to run forever. You learn yes eventually; you may never learn no. <bookmark mark='c'/> And it is co-recognizable if its complement is recognizable: a machine can confirm every no. <bookmark mark='d'/> The central example is K, the descriptions of machines that halt when given their own description. <bookmark mark='e'/> K is recognizable: just run the machine and say yes if it stops. That is the universal machine of Part 1. <bookmark mark='f'/> But it is not decidable; that was Part 1's diagonal argument.
72c92f965265.zh: 第1部分证明了停机问题不可判定。这一部分把这幅图画得更精确。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个语言是可判定的，如果有某台机器总会停机并正确回答是或否。<bookmark mark='b'/>它是可识别的，也叫递归可枚举，如果有某台机器对每个成员都停机并回答是，而对其余的允许永远运行下去。你终究会知道“是”；却可能永远不知道“否”。<bookmark mark='c'/>它是补可识别的，如果它的补集可识别：有机器能确认每一个“否”。<bookmark mark='d'/>核心的例子是 K：那些在得到自己的描述时会停机的机器的描述。<bookmark mark='e'/>K 是可识别的：只要运行这台机器，它一停就说是。那就是第1部分的通用机。<bookmark mark='f'/>但它不可判定；那是第1部分的对角线论证。

fb5aac04a10c.en: Draw the classes. <bookmark mark='a'/> Recognizable languages on the left, co-recognizable on the right. <bookmark mark='b'/> Their overlap is exactly the decidable languages. Given a recognizer for a language and one for its complement, run both side by side, a step of each in turn. Every input belongs to one side, so one of them stops, and you know the answer. <bookmark mark='c'/> K sits on the left. So its complement, the machines that run forever on themselves, cannot be recognizable, or K would be decidable. <bookmark mark='d'/> And some problems are on neither side. Whether a machine halts on every input, called TOT, cannot be confirmed either way by any finite amount of evidence. Chapter nine measures how far outside it lies.
fb5aac04a10c.zh: 把这些类画出来。<bookmark mark='a'/>左边是可识别语言，右边是补可识别语言。<bookmark mark='b'/>它们的交集恰好是可判定语言。给定一个语言的识别器和它补集的识别器，让两者轮流各走一步并排运行。每个输入都属于某一边，所以总有一个会停下，你就知道答案了。<bookmark mark='c'/>K 在左边。所以它的补集，也就是在自身上永远运行的机器，不可能是可识别的，否则 K 就可判定了。<bookmark mark='d'/>还有些问题哪一边都不在。一台机器是否在每个输入上都停机，叫作 TOT，任何有限的证据都无法从任何一方确认它。第9章会测量它在外面有多远。

0041fb8d1f02.en: Almost every impossibility proof after the first one is a reduction. <bookmark mark='a'/> A maps to B if a computable function f turns every question about A into a question about B with the same answer: members land inside B, and non-members land outside. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then a decider for B gives a decider for A: compute f, and ask. <bookmark mark='c'/> Read backwards, if A is undecidable, B must be too. To prove a new problem impossible, you show that the halting problem reduces to it.
0041fb8d1f02.zh: 第一个不可能性证明之后，几乎每一个都是归约。<bookmark mark='a'/>说 A 映射归约到 B，如果有一个可计算函数 f，把每个关于 A 的问题变成一个答案相同的关于 B 的问题：成员落在 B 里面，非成员落在外面。<bookmark mark='b'/>那么 B 的判定器就给出 A 的判定器：算出 f，再去问。<bookmark mark='c'/>倒过来读，如果 A 不可判定，B 也必然不可判定。要证明一个新问题不可能，就证明停机问题能归约到它。

6907f0bdd63f.en: Here is the start of the catalogue. <bookmark mark='a'/> Whether a machine accepts a given input is recognizable and undecidable, since K is the special case of a machine run on itself. Whether a machine accepts nothing at all is co-recognizable and undecidable. Whether two machines accept the same language is on neither side. And whether a machine halts on every input is further out still. <bookmark mark='b'/> The trick is always the same: build a new machine that ignores its own input and simulates the hard case. <bookmark mark='c'/> Here, a machine M prime that accepts everything if M accepts w, and nothing otherwise. Asking whether M prime accepts nothing is asking whether M accepts w. <bookmark mark='d'/> Doing this one problem at a time gets tedious. The next chapter does them all at once.
6907f0bdd63f.zh: 这是这份目录的开头。<bookmark mark='a'/>一台机器是否接受给定输入，是可识别而不可判定的，因为 K 就是把机器运行在它自身上的特例。一台机器是否什么都不接受，是补可识别而不可判定的。两台机器是否接受同一个语言，哪一边都不在。而一台机器是否在每个输入上都停机，离得更远。<bookmark mark='b'/>技巧总是同一个：造一台新机器，忽略它自己的输入，去模拟那个困难的情形。<bookmark mark='c'/>这里，造一台 M′：如果 M 接受 w，它就接受一切，否则什么都不接受。问 M′ 是否什么都不接受，就是在问 M 是否接受 w。<bookmark mark='d'/>一次只做一个问题很乏味。下一章一次把它们全做掉。

38ce49adc68b.en: Henry Rice proved in 1953 that the halting problem is not an isolated case but the rule. <bookmark mark='a'/> Call a property of programs semantic if it depends only on what the program computes, its input-output behaviour, and not on how it is written. <bookmark mark='b'/> Call it non-trivial if some programs have it and some do not. <bookmark mark='c'/> Halting on zero, never dividing by zero, computing a sorting function, being equivalent to a given program: all semantic, all non-trivial. <bookmark mark='d'/> Rice's theorem says every such property is undecidable. The proof is one construction. Suppose the program that never answers lacks the property, and some program Y has it. <bookmark mark='e'/> Given any machine M and input w, build M prime: on input x, first run M on w, and if that ever finishes, run Y on x. <bookmark mark='f'/> If M halts on w, M prime computes exactly what Y computes, so it has the property. If not, M prime never answers anything, so it lacks it. <bookmark mark='g'/> A decider for the property would decide halting. If the never-answering program has the property instead, apply the argument to its complement.
38ce49adc68b.zh: Henry Rice 在1953年证明，停机问题不是孤立的个案，而是常态。<bookmark mark='a'/>如果一个程序性质只取决于程序计算什么，即它的输入输出行为，而不取决于它怎么写，就称它是语义的。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果有些程序有它、有些没有，就称它是非平凡的。<bookmark mark='c'/>在零上停机，从不除以零，计算一个排序函数，与给定程序等价：全都是语义的，全都非平凡。<bookmark mark='d'/>Rice 定理说，每一个这样的性质都不可判定。证明只是一个构造。假设那个从不作答的程序没有这个性质，而某个程序 Y 有。<bookmark mark='e'/>给定任意机器 M 和输入 w，造出 M′：在输入 x 上，先在 w 上运行 M，如果它结束了，再在 x 上运行 Y。<bookmark mark='f'/>如果 M 在 w 上停机，M′ 计算的恰好就是 Y 所计算的，所以它有这个性质。否则 M′ 对什么都不作答，所以没有。<bookmark mark='g'/>这个性质的判定器就会判定停机。如果是那个从不作答的程序有这个性质，就把论证用在它的补上。

da1451e9648b.en: This shapes real software. <bookmark mark='a'/> Fred Cohen showed in 1987 that no program can detect every virus, since behaving maliciously is a semantic property. <bookmark mark='b'/> No compiler can always find the best equivalent program, or even all the dead code. <bookmark mark='c'/> And no static analyzer can be both sound, never missing a bug, and complete, never raising a false alarm. <bookmark mark='d'/> Practice escapes by approximating. A type checker rejects some correct programs, as Part 14 showed; analyzers err on the side of warnings. <bookmark mark='e'/> Or it restricts the language until the question becomes decidable, and Part 54 will prove real programs correct within such limits. <bookmark mark='f'/> Notice what Rice does not forbid. Questions about the text of a program, how many states it has or whether it contains a loop, remain easy.
da1451e9648b.zh: 这塑造了真实的软件。<bookmark mark='a'/>Fred Cohen 在1987年证明，没有程序能检测出每一种病毒，因为行为恶意是一个语义性质。<bookmark mark='b'/>没有编译器总能找到最好的等价程序，甚至找不全所有的死代码。<bookmark mark='c'/>也没有静态分析器能既可靠，从不漏掉 bug，又完备，从不误报。<bookmark mark='d'/>实践靠近似逃出去。类型检查器会拒绝一些正确的程序，正如第14部分所示；分析器宁可多报警告。<bookmark mark='e'/>或者限制语言，直到问题变得可判定，第54部分会在这样的限制之内证明真实程序的正确性。<bookmark mark='f'/>注意 Rice 没有禁止什么。关于程序文本的问题，它有多少个状态，是否含有循环，仍然很容易。

9894a0a78da3.en: Chapter four. Programs that know their own code.
9894a0a78da3.zh: 第4章。知道自己代码的程序。

c9b20243c921.en: Can a program print its own source? The obvious attempt fails: a print statement must contain its own text, which contains the print statement, forever. <bookmark mark='a'/> The trick is to split the program in two. Here in Python, the string s is a template of the whole program, with a hole. The print statement fills the hole with the string itself, quoted. <bookmark mark='b'/> Our Pebble language has no string formatting, so its quine is longer: seven hundred and fifty-nine lines. Most of them store the rest of the program as numbers, one character each. <bookmark mark='c'/> The tail then prints the head from that data, then prints each assignment statement, then prints the tail. Part A describes part B; part B prints A twice, once as code and once as the text it encodes. <bookmark mark='d'/> We ran it on the emulator: ninety-nine thousand instructions, and the output is the source, byte for byte.
c9b20243c921.zh: 一个程序能打印出自己的源代码吗？最直接的尝试会失败：打印语句必须包含自己的文本，而那段文本又包含打印语句，没完没了。<bookmark mark='a'/>诀窍是把程序拆成两半。在这个 Python 例子里，字符串 s 是整个程序的模板，留着一个洞。打印语句用加了引号的字符串自己去填这个洞。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们的 Pebble 语言没有字符串格式化，所以它的自打印程序更长：七百五十九行。其中大多数行把程序的其余部分存成数字，每个字符一个。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后尾部先从这些数据打印出头部，再打印每一条赋值语句，最后打印尾部。A 部分描述 B 部分；B 部分把 A 打印两遍，一遍作为代码，一遍作为它所编码的文本。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们在模拟器上运行了它：九万九千条指令，输出就是源代码，逐字节相同。

7b2bbacc129b.en: Stephen Kleene turned the trick into a theorem in 1938. <bookmark mark='a'/> For any computable way of transforming programs, there is a program that behaves exactly like its own transform. <bookmark mark='b'/> In practice: a program can always obtain its own description, and then do whatever it likes with it. <bookmark mark='c'/> The quine is the simplest case, where the program just prints the text. <bookmark mark='d'/> Here is the halting problem again, in three lines. Suppose H decides halting. Write a program R that gets its own code, asks H whether R halts, and then does the opposite: loops if H says halt, halts if H says loop. H is wrong about R. <bookmark mark='e'/> No diagonal table, no list of all machines: self-reference is simply a programming technique. <bookmark mark='f'/> It is the same trick that powers self-replicating viruses, Gödel's self-referential sentence in chapter eight, and Ken Thompson's trojan compiler, which Part 55 will build and catch.
7b2bbacc129b.zh: Stephen Kleene 在1938年把这个诀窍变成了定理。<bookmark mark='a'/>对于任何可计算的程序变换方式，都有一个程序的行为与它自己的变换结果完全一样。<bookmark mark='b'/>在实践中：一个程序总能得到自己的描述，然后拿它做任何想做的事。<bookmark mark='c'/>自打印程序是最简单的情形，程序只是把文本打印出来。<bookmark mark='d'/>这里用三行再讲一次停机问题。假设 H 能判定停机。写一个程序 R：取得自己的代码，问 H R 是否停机，然后反着做：H 说停机它就循环，H 说循环它就停机。H 在 R 上错了。<bookmark mark='e'/>不需要对角线表格，也不需要列出所有机器：自指只是一种编程技巧。<bookmark mark='f'/>正是同一个诀窍驱动着自我复制的病毒、第8章里 Gödel 的自指语句，以及 Ken Thompson 的特洛伊编译器，第55部分会把它造出来再抓住它。

078dcf5754c1.en: Here is a puzzle with no machines in it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each domino has a string on top and a string below. You may use as many copies of each as you like, in any order, and you win if the top row and the bottom row spell the same string. <bookmark mark='b'/> For these four, a search finds a match of five dominoes: two, one, three, two, four. <bookmark mark='c'/> Both rows read a b c a a a b c. <bookmark mark='d'/> Post's correspondence problem asks, for any finite set of dominoes, whether a match exists. <bookmark mark='e'/> Emil Post proved in 1946 that no algorithm can answer it. A search confirms a match when it finds one, but nothing can confirm in general that there is none.
078dcf5754c1.zh: 这是一个里面没有机器的谜题。<bookmark mark='a'/>每张多米诺上面有一个字符串，下面有一个字符串。每种你想用几张就用几张，顺序随意，如果上面一行和下面一行拼出同一个字符串，你就赢了。<bookmark mark='b'/>对这四张，搜索找到一个五张的匹配：二、一、三、二、四。<bookmark mark='c'/>两行读出来都是 a b c a a a b c。<bookmark mark='d'/>Post 对应问题问的是：对任意一组有限的多米诺，匹配是否存在。<bookmark mark='e'/>Emil Post 在1946年证明，没有算法能回答它。搜索找到匹配时能确认它，但一般而言，没有什么能确认匹配不存在。

4fd3c704246b.en: Why are dominoes as hard as machines? <bookmark mark='a'/> Take a tiny Turing machine: in state q, reading a one, it moves right into state p; in p, reading a zero, it accepts. <bookmark mark='b'/> We turn it into dominoes. The start domino has a single hash on top and the whole first configuration below. Step dominoes rewrite the head's neighbourhood. Copy dominoes carry the rest of the tape across. Clean-up dominoes let the accept state swallow the tape, and a last domino closes the rows. <bookmark mark='c'/> The bottom row is always one configuration ahead of the top, so the only way for the top to catch up is to write the next configuration, step by step. <bookmark mark='d'/> Our search found the thirteen-domino match. Read between the hashes: q one zero, then one p zero, then one zero a. That is the machine's accepting run. <bookmark mark='e'/> A match exists exactly when the machine accepts, so an algorithm for dominoes would decide acceptance. Sipser's textbook adds one more trick to force the start domino first; the idea is all here.
4fd3c704246b.zh: 为什么多米诺和机器一样难？<bookmark mark='a'/>拿一台很小的图灵机：在状态 q 读到一，它向右移动进入状态 p；在 p 读到零，它接受。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们把它变成多米诺。起始多米诺上面只有一个井号，下面是整个第一个格局。步骤多米诺改写读写头附近的内容。复制多米诺把纸带其余部分搬过去。清理多米诺让接受状态把纸带吞掉，最后一张多米诺把两行收尾。<bookmark mark='c'/>下面一行总比上面领先一个格局，所以上面要追上，唯一的办法就是一步一步写出下一个格局。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们的搜索找到了十三张的匹配。读井号之间的内容：q 一 零，然后一 p 零，然后一 零 a。那就是这台机器的接受过程。<bookmark mark='e'/>匹配存在当且仅当机器接受，所以多米诺的算法就会判定接受。Sipser 的教科书再加一个小技巧，强制起始多米诺放在最前面；思想都在这里了。

b89b42ac8f3d.en: How does undecidability show up in practice? <bookmark mark='a'/> We drew twenty thousand random sets of three dominoes, each string one to three bits long. Most have no match the search can find; of those that do, most matches are a single domino. <bookmark mark='b'/> The longest shortest match we drew was fifteen dominoes. <bookmark mark='c'/> But these four dominoes, found by enthusiasts who hunt for hard instances, have no match shorter than two hundred and six, and our search confirmed it. There is no computable bound on how long the shortest match can be; if there were, we could search up to the bound and decide the problem. <bookmark mark='d'/> Where exactly does it become impossible? With two dominoes the problem is decidable, a 1982 theorem. With five or more it is undecidable, proved by Turlough Neary in 2015. <bookmark mark='e'/> Three and four are open.
b89b42ac8f3d.zh: 不可判定性在实践中是什么样子？<bookmark mark='a'/>我们随机抽了两万组三张的多米诺，每个字符串一到三位。大多数没有搜索能找到的匹配；有匹配的那些，大多只用一张多米诺。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们抽到的最长的最短匹配是十五张。<bookmark mark='c'/>但这四张多米诺，是专门搜寻困难实例的爱好者找到的，它们最短的匹配也要两百零六张，我们的搜索证实了这一点。最短匹配能有多长，没有可计算的上界；如果有，我们只要搜索到那个上界就能判定这个问题。<bookmark mark='d'/>到底从哪里开始变得不可能？两张多米诺时问题可判定，这是1982年的定理。五张或更多时不可判定，由 Turlough Neary 在2015年证明。<bookmark mark='e'/>三张和四张仍是未解之谜。

d0fe00ee0a46.en: Part 12 promised a proof that nobody can always detect an ambiguous grammar. Here it is. <bookmark mark='a'/> From any set of dominoes, build this grammar. T derives the tops of some sequence of dominoes, followed by the sequence's numbers in reverse. B does the same with the bottoms. <bookmark mark='b'/> The markers at the end record exactly which dominoes were used, so neither half is ambiguous by itself. <bookmark mark='c'/> A string has two parse trees only if one comes through T and one through B, with the same markers: the same dominoes, whose tops spell the same string as their bottoms. That is a match. <bookmark mark='d'/> So the grammar is ambiguous exactly when the dominoes match, and deciding ambiguity would decide Post's problem. <bookmark mark='e'/> The same construction shows that whether two grammars share a string, or whether a grammar generates every string, is undecidable too. Parser generators warn about conflicts instead; that is an approximation, in the spirit of Rice.
d0fe00ee0a46.zh: 第12部分许诺过一个证明：没有人总能检测出有歧义的文法。就在这里。<bookmark mark='a'/>从任意一组多米诺出发，造出这个文法。T 推导出某个多米诺序列的上半部分，后面跟着这个序列编号的倒序。B 对下半部分做同样的事。<bookmark mark='b'/>末尾的标记准确记录了用了哪些多米诺，所以每一半本身都没有歧义。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个字符串有两棵语法树，只可能一棵经由 T，一棵经由 B，且标记相同：同样的多米诺，上半部分拼出的字符串与下半部分相同。那就是一个匹配。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以文法有歧义当且仅当多米诺有匹配，判定歧义就会判定 Post 的问题。<bookmark mark='e'/>同样的构造还说明，两个文法是否有公共字符串，或者一个文法是否生成所有字符串，也都不可判定。语法分析器生成器于是改为报告冲突；那是一种近似，带着 Rice 的精神。

f713888ead34.en: In 1961 Hao Wang asked a question about square tiles with coloured edges. <bookmark mark='a'/> You may not rotate them, and wherever two tiles touch, the edge colours must agree. Given a finite set, can copies of it cover the whole plane? <bookmark mark='b'/> For these eleven, a backtracking search finds squares easily: twelve by twelve in forty-five thousand tries, twenty by twenty in four million. <bookmark mark='c'/> Wang conjectured that any set that tiles the plane can also tile it periodically, with a pattern that repeats. A periodic tiling folds up onto a torus, so we searched every small torus. Every one we could finish was impossible. <bookmark mark='d'/> That is because these are Emmanuel Jeandel and Michael Rao's eleven tiles from 2015: they tile the plane, but never periodically, and they proved no smaller set can do that.
f713888ead34.zh: 1961年，王浩问了一个关于边缘涂色的正方形砖的问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>不许旋转，两块砖相接的地方，边的颜色必须一致。给定一组有限的砖，它们的复制品能铺满整个平面吗？<bookmark mark='b'/>对这十一块，回溯搜索很容易找到正方形拼片：十二乘十二用了四万五千次尝试，二十乘二十用了四百万次。<bookmark mark='c'/>王浩猜想，任何能铺满平面的砖组，也能用一个重复的图案周期性地铺满。周期性的铺砌可以折叠到环面上，所以我们搜索了每一个小环面。每一个能搜完的都不可能。<bookmark mark='d'/>那是因为这些正是 Emmanuel Jeandel 和 Michael Rao 在2015年给出的十一块砖：它们能铺满平面，但永远不是周期性的，而且他们证明了没有更小的砖组能做到这一点。

cf2f702c9742.en: Why should tiles be hard? <bookmark mark='a'/> Write a Turing machine's run as a table, one row per step, each row the tape at that moment, with the state marked on the head's cell. Make a tile for each kind of cell. <bookmark mark='b'/> Choose the edge colours so that a row of tiles can only be followed by the row that is the machine's next step. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then the tiles can fill the plane exactly when the machine runs forever, and deciding tiling would decide halting. <bookmark mark='d'/> Robert Berger proved this in 1966. The hard part was forcing the computation to happen everywhere at every scale, which needed a set that tiles only aperiodically. His had twenty thousand four hundred and twenty-six tiles. <bookmark mark='e'/> Raphael Robinson brought it to six shapes, Roger Penrose to two, Jarkko Kari and Karel Culik to thirteen Wang tiles, and Jeandel and Rao to eleven.
cf2f702c9742.zh: 砖块为什么会难？<bookmark mark='a'/>把一台图灵机的运行写成一张表，每一步一行，每一行是那一时刻的纸带，读写头所在的格子标上状态。为每一种格子做一块砖。<bookmark mark='b'/>选好边的颜色，使一行砖后面只能接上代表机器下一步的那一行。<bookmark mark='c'/>那么这些砖能铺满平面，恰好当机器永远运行，判定铺砌就会判定停机。<bookmark mark='d'/>Robert Berger 在1966年证明了这一点。难点在于强迫计算在每个地方、每个尺度上都发生，这需要一组只能非周期地铺砌的砖。他的那组有两万零四百二十六块。<bookmark mark='e'/>Raphael Robinson 把它降到六种形状，Roger Penrose 降到两种，Jarkko Kari 和 Karel Culik 降到十三块 Wang 砖，Jeandel 和 Rao 降到十一块。

935e9d8ebe00.en: The sequence ended in 2023, with an amateur. <bookmark mark='a'/> David Smith, a retired print technician who played with shapes, found a single tile that covers the plane, but only aperiodically. With Joseph Myers, Craig Kaplan and Chaim Goodman-Strauss he proved it. <bookmark mark='b'/> It is called the hat: thirteen vertices, eight kites cut from a hexagonal grid. <bookmark mark='c'/> The hat needs reflected copies as well; two months later the same team found the spectre, which does not. <bookmark mark='d'/> It answered the einstein problem, German for one stone, which had been open since Berger's aperiodic sets. <bookmark mark='e'/> And it is still true that no algorithm can tell, for an arbitrary finite set of tiles, whether it covers the plane.
935e9d8ebe00.zh: 这个序列在2023年由一位业余爱好者画上了句号。<bookmark mark='a'/>David Smith，一位喜欢摆弄形状的退休印刷技师，找到了一块单独的砖，能铺满平面，但只能非周期地铺。他和 Joseph Myers、Craig Kaplan、Chaim Goodman-Strauss 一起证明了它。<bookmark mark='b'/>它叫作“帽子”：十三个顶点，由六边形网格切出的八个风筝形组成。<bookmark mark='c'/>帽子还需要它的镜像；两个月后，同一个团队找到了“幽灵”，它不需要镜像。<bookmark mark='d'/>它回答了“einstein 问题”，德语意思是“一块石头”，这个问题自 Berger 的非周期砖组以来一直悬而未决。<bookmark mark='e'/>而且仍然成立的是：对任意一组有限的砖，没有算法能判断它能否铺满平面。

48bf9c859e5f.zh: 第7章。希尔伯特第十问题。

0acc1d6f1702.en: In 1900 David Hilbert asked for a process that decides, for any polynomial equation with integer coefficients, whether it has a solution in integers. <bookmark mark='a'/> Pell's equation shows why searching is not enough. For D equal to thirteen, the smallest solution has x equal to six hundred and forty-nine; for sixty-one, a ten-digit number; for nine hundred and ninety-one, thirty digits. <bookmark mark='b'/> Brute force over y finds thirteen's in a hundred and eighty tries and twenty-nine's in eighteen hundred, but for sixty-one, seventy-eight million tries in twenty seconds find nothing. <bookmark mark='c'/> For Pell's equation we are lucky: continued fractions find the answer at once, and Lagrange proved one always exists. <bookmark mark='d'/> In general a search that has found nothing has proved nothing. The answer could be further out, or there could be none. Hilbert hoped for a method that always knows which.
0acc1d6f1702.zh: 1900年，David Hilbert 要求一种过程，对任何整系数多项式方程，判定它是否有整数解。<bookmark mark='a'/>Pell 方程说明了为什么搜索不够。D 等于十三时，最小解的 x 是六百四十九；六十一时，是一个十位数；九百九十一时，三十位。<bookmark mark='b'/>对 y 暴力搜索，十三的解要一百八十次尝试，二十九的要一千八百次，而六十一，二十秒里七千八百万次尝试一无所获。<bookmark mark='c'/>对 Pell 方程我们很幸运：连分数立刻就能找到答案，而且 Lagrange 证明了解总是存在。<bookmark mark='d'/>但一般来说，一次一无所获的搜索什么也没证明。答案可能在更远处，也可能根本没有。Hilbert 希望有一种方法，总能知道是哪一种。

17bc8a692f58.en: The answer took seventy years and four people. <bookmark mark='a'/> Call a set of numbers Diophantine if it is exactly the set of parameters for which some polynomial equation has a solution. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 1961 Martin Davis, Hilary Putnam and Julia Robinson proved that every recognizable set is Diophantine, provided that exponentiation is. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 1970 Yuri Matiyasevich, aged twenty-two, closed the gap: the relation y equals two to the x is Diophantine, with a construction built on the Fibonacci numbers. <bookmark mark='d'/> So the recognizable sets and the Diophantine sets are the same. <bookmark mark='e'/> In particular there is a polynomial that has a solution exactly when machine number n halts on itself. <bookmark mark='f'/> A process for Hilbert's problem would decide halting. There is none.
17bc8a692f58.zh: 答案用了七十年和四个人。<bookmark mark='a'/>如果一个数集恰好是使某个多项式方程有解的参数之集，就称它是丢番图集。<bookmark mark='b'/>1961年，Martin Davis、Hilary Putnam 和 Julia Robinson 证明，只要指数运算是丢番图的，每个可识别集就都是丢番图集。<bookmark mark='c'/>1970年，二十二岁的 Yuri Matiyasevich 补上了缺口：关系 y 等于二的 x 次方是丢番图的，构造建立在斐波那契数之上。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以可识别集和丢番图集是同一回事。<bookmark mark='e'/>特别地，存在一个多项式，它有解恰好当第 n 号机器在自身上停机。<bookmark mark='f'/>Hilbert 问题的过程就会判定停机。这样的过程不存在。

fa2d7aa02243.en: A striking corollary. <bookmark mark='a'/> The primes are a recognizable set, so they are Diophantine, and James Jones, Daihachiro Sato, Hideo Wada and Douglas Wiens wrote the polynomial out in 1976: twenty-six variables, one for each letter of the alphabet, degree twenty-five. <bookmark mark='b'/> Plug in any non-negative integers. Whenever the value is positive, it is a prime, and every prime appears. <bookmark mark='c'/> The trick is the shape: k plus two, times one minus a sum of squares. That is positive only when every square is zero, that is, when fourteen equations hold at once, and they hold exactly when k plus two is prime. <bookmark mark='d'/> Nobody would find primes this way; random inputs give negative values almost always. The point is that primality, like halting, can be written as a single equation.
fa2d7aa02243.zh: 一个惊人的推论。<bookmark mark='a'/>素数是一个可识别集，所以它是丢番图的，James Jones、佐藤大八郎、和田秀男和 Douglas Wiens 在1976年把这个多项式写了出来：二十六个变量，字母表里每个字母一个，次数二十五。<bookmark mark='b'/>代入任意非负整数。只要值是正的，它就是素数，而且每个素数都会出现。<bookmark mark='c'/>诀窍在于它的形状：k 加二，乘以一减去一串平方和。这只在每个平方都为零时为正，也就是十四个方程同时成立时，而它们成立恰好当 k 加二是素数。<bookmark mark='d'/>没人会这样找素数；随机输入几乎总给出负值。要点在于，素性和停机一样，可以写成一个方程。

2a5939d2fe20.zh: 第8章。经由停机问题的 Gödel。

cca6dd2192be.en: In 1931 Kurt Gödel needed arithmetic to talk about itself. <bookmark mark='a'/> Give every symbol a code number. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then encode a formula as a product of prime powers: two to the code of the first symbol, times three to the code of the second, and so on. Zero equals zero is two times twenty-seven times five: two hundred and seventy. A short statement that adding zero changes nothing has forty-seven digits. <bookmark mark='c'/> Factoring recovers the formula, so nothing is lost. <bookmark mark='d'/> A proof is a list of formulas, so it has a number too, and whether one number is a proof of another is a mechanical check. Part 1 did the same for machines, with description strings. Gödel did it first, for logic.
cca6dd2192be.zh: 1931年，Kurt Gödel 需要让算术谈论它自己。<bookmark mark='a'/>给每个符号一个编码数。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后把一个公式编码成素数幂的乘积：二的第一个符号编码次方，乘以三的第二个符号编码次方，依此类推。零等于零是二乘二十七乘五：两百七十。一句“加零什么都不改变”的短陈述有四十七位。<bookmark mark='c'/>因式分解就能还原公式，所以什么都没丢。<bookmark mark='d'/>证明是一串公式，所以它也有一个编号，而一个数是否是另一个数的证明，是一项机械的检查。第1部分对机器做过同样的事，用的是描述字符串。Gödel 最先为逻辑做了这件事。

5818414f583d.en: Here is Gödel's first theorem, proved from Part 1's result in a minute. <bookmark mark='a'/> A theory is a set of axioms and rules of proof, mechanical enough that a program can list all its theorems. <bookmark mark='b'/> Suppose it is sound, proving only true things, and strong enough to state that a machine halts on an input. Ordinary arithmetic is. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now suppose it could prove every true statement of the form, machine M does not halt on w. <bookmark mark='d'/> Then we could decide halting. Run M on w, and at the same time list the theorems, looking for M does not halt. <bookmark mark='e'/> If M halts, the run finishes. If it does not, the proof turns up. Either way we get an answer, and soundness makes it correct. <bookmark mark='f'/> That cannot be. So there are true statements, that some machine runs forever, which the theory cannot prove. Every sound theory of arithmetic is incomplete.
5818414f583d.zh: 这是 Gödel 第一定理，用第1部分的结果一分钟就能证明。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个理论是一组公理和证明规则，机械到一个程序能列出它的全部定理。<bookmark mark='b'/>假设它是可靠的，只证明真的东西，并且强到能陈述一台机器在某个输入上停机。普通算术就可以。<bookmark mark='c'/>再假设它能证明每一条形如“机器 M 在 w 上不停机”的真命题。<bookmark mark='d'/>那我们就能判定停机。在 w 上运行 M，同时列举定理，寻找“M 不停机”。<bookmark mark='e'/>如果 M 停机，运行会结束。如果不停机，证明会出现。无论哪种我们都得到答案，而可靠性保证它正确。<bookmark mark='f'/>这不可能。所以存在真命题，说某台机器永远运行，而这个理论无法证明。每一个可靠的算术理论都是不完备的。

b646df769f9b.en: The proof says some such statement exists. The recursion theorem lets us write it down. <bookmark mark='a'/> Program R obtains its own source, the trick of chapter four, and then searches through every proof in the theory, shortest first, for a proof that R never halts. If it finds one, it stops. <bookmark mark='b'/> If the theory proved that R never halts, R would find the proof and halt, and the theory would have proved something false. <bookmark mark='c'/> So a sound theory never proves it, R searches forever, and the statement R never halts is true, and unprovable. <bookmark mark='d'/> It says, in effect, I cannot be proved: Gödel's sentence, as a program. <bookmark mark='e'/> Gödel's own version needed less: only that the theory be consistent, with a refinement by Barkley Rosser in 1936.
b646df769f9b.zh: 证明说这样的命题存在。递归定理让我们把它写出来。<bookmark mark='a'/>程序 R 取得自己的源代码，也就是第4章的诀窍，然后从短到长搜索理论中的每个证明，寻找“R 永不停机”的证明。找到了，它就停下。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果理论证明了 R 永不停机，R 就会找到这个证明并停机，理论就证明了一件假的事。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以可靠的理论永远不会证明它，R 永远搜索下去，而“R 永不停机”这个命题是真的，也是不可证的。<bookmark mark='d'/>它实际上在说：我不能被证明。这就是写成程序的 Gödel 语句。<bookmark mark='e'/>Gödel 自己的版本要求更少：只需理论是一致的，再加上 Barkley Rosser 在1936年的一个改进。

df79dd74e6f0.en: Push one step further. <bookmark mark='a'/> The argument we just gave can itself be carried out inside the theory. The theory can prove: if I am consistent, then R never halts. <bookmark mark='b'/> So if it could also prove its own consistency, it would prove that R never halts, which we just saw it cannot do. <bookmark mark='c'/> That is the second incompleteness theorem: no consistent theory strong enough for arithmetic proves its own consistency. <bookmark mark='d'/> It ended the program David Hilbert had led in the 1920s, to prove all of mathematics consistent by finite, mechanical means. <bookmark mark='e'/> Notice the shape of the statement. The consistency of set theory says that one program, the one hunting for a contradiction, never halts. <bookmark mark='f'/> And that is why Part 1 could build a Turing machine whose busy-beaver value set theory cannot determine. Chapter twelve comes back to it.
df79dd74e6f0.zh: 再推进一步。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们刚才的论证本身可以在理论内部进行。理论能证明：如果我是一致的，那么 R 永不停机。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以如果它还能证明自己的一致性，它就能证明 R 永不停机，而我们刚看到它做不到。<bookmark mark='c'/>这就是第二不完备定理：没有一个强到足以做算术的一致理论能证明自己的一致性。<bookmark mark='d'/>它终结了 David Hilbert 在1920年代领导的纲领：用有限的、机械的手段证明全部数学的一致性。<bookmark mark='e'/>注意这个命题的形状。集合论的一致性说的是：某一个程序，那个寻找矛盾的程序，永不停机。<bookmark mark='f'/>这就是为什么第1部分能造出一台图灵机，它的忙碌海狸值集合论无法确定。第12章会回到这里。

c64f75143337.en: Chapter nine. Oracles and the arithmetic hierarchy.

6e10cabceb77.en: Is halting the hardest problem there is? <bookmark mark='a'/> Turing asked in 1939 what a machine could do with a magic box, an oracle, that answers membership in some set in a single step. A problem is Turing-reducible to B if a machine with an oracle for B solves it. <bookmark mark='b'/> Give a machine the halting set as its oracle. Every question of the form, does some search succeed, is now one step. <bookmark mark='c'/> But Part 1's diagonal argument works just as well for oracle machines: they cannot decide whether oracle machines halt. That is a new, harder problem, the jump of K. <bookmark mark='d'/> Give that an oracle and jump again. There is an infinite tower of problems, each strictly harder than the last.
6e10cabceb77.zh: 停机是最难的问题吗？<bookmark mark='a'/>Turing 在1939年问：如果一台机器有一个魔盒，一个谕示，能一步回答某个集合的成员资格，它能做什么？如果一台带 B 谕示的机器能解一个问题，就说这个问题图灵归约到 B。<bookmark mark='b'/>把停机集作为谕示交给一台机器。每一个形如“某个搜索会成功吗”的问题，现在都只是一步。<bookmark mark='c'/>但第1部分的对角线论证对谕示机同样有效：它们无法判定谕示机是否停机。那是一个新的、更难的问题，K 的跳跃。<bookmark mark='d'/>再给它一个谕示，再跳一次。有一座无限的问题之塔，每一个都严格比前一个更难。

eee7657de15f.en: There is a ruler for this tower: count the alternating quantifiers. <bookmark mark='a'/> At the bottom, questions a program settles by bounded search: is x prime, does M halt within a hundred steps. <bookmark mark='b'/> One existential quantifier in front, there exists a time t at which M has halted, gives sigma one: halting itself, and the equations of chapter seven. <bookmark mark='c'/> One universal quantifier gives pi one: M never halts. So do Goldbach's conjecture and the Riemann hypothesis, and the consistency of set theory; each says some search never succeeds. <bookmark mark='d'/> Two quantifiers. Halting on only finitely many inputs is sigma two. <bookmark mark='e'/> Halting on every input, TOT, is pi two: for every input, there is a time. So are the twin prime conjecture, the Collatz conjecture, and P not equal to NP, the subject of Part 26. <bookmark mark='f'/> And halting on all but finitely many inputs is sigma three. <bookmark mark='g'/> Emil Post proved in 1948 that each level is exactly what a recognizer can do with an oracle for the jump below, and each of these machine problems is complete for its level.
eee7657de15f.zh: 这座塔有一把尺子：数交替出现的量词。<bookmark mark='a'/>最底层是程序靠有界搜索就能解决的问题：x 是素数吗，M 在一百步内停机吗。<bookmark mark='b'/>前面加一个存在量词，存在一个时刻 t 使 M 已经停机，就得到 sigma 一：停机本身，以及第7章的方程。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个全称量词给出pi 一：M 永不停机。Goldbach 猜想和黎曼猜想也是，集合论的一致性也是；每一个都说某个搜索永远不会成功。<bookmark mark='d'/>两个量词。只在有限多个输入上停机是 sigma 二。<bookmark mark='e'/>在每个输入上都停机，TOT，是 pi 二：对每个输入，都有一个时刻。孪生素数猜想、Collatz 猜想，以及 P 不等于 NP 也是，后者正是第26部分的主题。<bookmark mark='f'/>而在除有限多个以外的所有输入上停机是 sigma 三。<bookmark mark='g'/>Emil Post 在1948年证明，每一层恰好是识别器借助下一层跳跃的谕示所能做的，而这些机器问题在各自的层级上都是完全的。

eefd5572bb1e.en: One last question about the recognizable sets. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every undecidable one we have met so far is exactly as hard as halting. Is that always so? <bookmark mark='b'/> Emil Post asked in 1944, and it took twelve years. Albert Muchnik in Moscow and Richard Friedberg, an undergraduate at Harvard, independently built two recognizable sets, neither of which can compute the other, so both lie strictly between the decidable sets and K. <bookmark mark='c'/> Their technique, the priority method, builds the sets in stages, satisfying an infinite list of requirements, each one disturbed only finitely often by those ranked above it. <bookmark mark='d'/> Gerald Sacks showed later that between any two such degrees there is another: the structure is dense. <bookmark mark='e'/> And yet every natural problem anyone has found is either decidable or exactly as hard as halting. Nobody knows why.
eefd5572bb1e.zh: 关于可识别集的最后一个问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>到目前为止我们遇到的每一个不可判定集，都恰好和停机一样难。总是这样吗？<bookmark mark='b'/>Emil Post 在1944年提出这个问题，花了十二年才解决。莫斯科的 Albert Muchnik 和哈佛的本科生 Richard Friedberg 各自独立地造出两个可识别集，谁也不能计算对方，所以两者都严格位于可判定集和 K 之间。<bookmark mark='c'/>他们的技术，优先方法，分阶段构造这些集合，满足一张无限的要求清单，每个要求只被排在它前面的要求干扰有限多次。<bookmark mark='d'/>Gerald Sacks 后来证明，任意两个这样的度之间都还有另一个：这个结构是稠密的。<bookmark mark='e'/>然而人们找到的每一个自然问题，要么可判定，要么恰好和停机一样难。没人知道为什么。

3de22d2803ec.en: Andrey Kolmogorov, Ray Solomonoff and Gregory Chaitin, independently in the 1960s, measured information by programs. <bookmark mark='a'/> The Kolmogorov complexity of a string is the length of the shortest program that prints it. <bookmark mark='b'/> Compressors give a feel for it. We gave three of them a hundred thousand bytes of six kinds. Random bytes do not shrink at all; the output is slightly larger. <bookmark mark='c'/> English text shrinks to about a third. The digits of pi to forty-three percent, which is just the cost of writing a digit in binary. <bookmark mark='d'/> But pi's digits are not random in Kolmogorov's sense: a nineteen-line function prints all of them. The compressors cannot find that program. <bookmark mark='e'/> Every compressor gives an upper bound on the complexity, never the value itself, and this chapter shows why nothing can do better.
3de22d2803ec.zh: Andrey Kolmogorov、Ray Solomonoff 和 Gregory Chaitin 在1960年代各自独立地用程序来度量信息。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个字符串的 Kolmogorov 复杂度，是打印它的最短程序的长度。<bookmark mark='b'/>压缩器能让人感受一下它。我们给三个压缩器各喂了六种十万字节的数据。随机字节完全缩不了；输出反而略大。<bookmark mark='c'/>英文文本缩到约三分之一。圆周率的数字缩到百分之四十三，那恰好是用二进制写一个数字的代价。<bookmark mark='d'/>但在 Kolmogorov 的意义上，圆周率的数字并不随机：一个十九行的函数就能把它们全部打印出来。压缩器找不到那个程序。<bookmark mark='e'/>每个压缩器给出的都是复杂度的上界，而不是它的值，这一章会说明为什么没有什么能做得更好。

96463e3f7a56.en: Shortest program in which language? <bookmark mark='a'/> The invariance theorem says it barely matters. For any two universal machines, complexities differ by at most a constant. <bookmark mark='b'/> The proof: U is universal, so some fixed program makes U interpret V. <bookmark mark='c'/> Put that interpreter in front of the shortest V-program for x, and you have a U-program for x, longer by the interpreter's length and no more. <bookmark mark='d'/> Swap the roles, and the two measures agree up to a constant. <bookmark mark='e'/> So the information in a string belongs to the string. <bookmark mark='f'/> Between Python and the Pebble language, the constant is the size of an interpreter for one written in the other.
96463e3f7a56.zh: 用哪种语言的最短程序？<bookmark mark='a'/>不变性定理说，这几乎无关紧要。对任意两台通用机，复杂度至多相差一个常数。<bookmark mark='b'/>证明：U 是通用的，所以某个固定的程序能让 U 解释 V。<bookmark mark='c'/>把这个解释器放在 x 的最短 V 程序前面，就得到 x 的一个 U 程序，只比原来多出解释器的长度。<bookmark mark='d'/>交换角色，两种度量就相差不超过一个常数。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以一个字符串里的信息属于这个字符串本身。<bookmark mark='f'/>在 Python 和 Pebble 语言之间，这个常数就是用其中一种写的另一种的解释器的大小。

2b88162d36d3.en: Now a proof that takes a single line. <bookmark mark='a'/> Count programs. There is one of length zero, two of length one, four of length two. All the programs shorter than n bits together number two to the n, minus one: fewer than the strings of length n. <bookmark mark='b'/> More generally, programs shorter than n minus k bits can print at most a two to the minus k fraction of the strings of length n. <bookmark mark='c'/> At most one string in a thousand and twenty-four can be shortened by ten bits, and at every length some string cannot be shortened at all. <bookmark mark='d'/> Such a string is called random: it has no description shorter than itself. It also shows that every compressor makes some file bigger, as it did for our random bytes.
2b88162d36d3.zh: 现在是一个只要一行的证明。<bookmark mark='a'/>数一数程序。长度为零的有一个，长度为一的有两个，长度为二的有四个。所有短于 n 位的程序加起来是二的 n 次方减一个：比长度为 n 的字符串少。<bookmark mark='b'/>更一般地，短于 n 减 k 位的程序，至多只能打印出长度为 n 的字符串中二的负 k 次方那么大的比例。<bookmark mark='c'/>一千零二十四个字符串中至多一个能缩短十位，而在每种长度上，都有某个字符串根本缩不短。<bookmark mark='d'/>这样的字符串称为随机的：它没有比自身更短的描述。这也说明，每个压缩器都会把某些文件变大，就像我们的随机字节那样。

3c1b708ee82e.en: Now the twist. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1906 Bertrand Russell published a paradox he credited to a librarian, G. G. Berry: the smallest number that cannot be named in under sixty letters. That phrase names it in fewer. Turn the paradox into a program. <bookmark mark='b'/> If complexity were computable, this function would return the first string whose complexity exceeds L. <bookmark mark='c'/> But the function, with the number L written into it, is only about log L bits long, plus a constant, and for large L that is much less than L. <bookmark mark='d'/> A short program would have printed a string that has no short program. So complexity cannot be computed. <bookmark mark='e'/> Gregory Chaitin pushed this into logic. Instead of computing K, search a sound theory's proofs for a proof that some string has complexity above L. <bookmark mark='f'/> The same argument shows the search must fail once L passes a constant that depends on the theory. Almost every string is random, and beyond a fixed size, no theory can prove a single one of them is.
3c1b708ee82e.zh: 现在是转折。<bookmark mark='a'/>1906年，Bertrand Russell 发表了一个他归功于图书管理员 G. G. Berry 的悖论：不能用少于六十个字母命名的最小的数。这句话用更少的字母命名了它。把这个悖论变成程序。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果复杂度可计算，这个函数就会返回第一个复杂度超过 L 的字符串。<bookmark mark='c'/>但把数 L 写进去之后，这个函数只有大约 log L 位，再加一个常数，而 L 很大时这远小于 L。<bookmark mark='d'/>一个短程序打印出了一个没有短程序的字符串。所以复杂度无法计算。<bookmark mark='e'/>Gregory Chaitin 把这一点推进到逻辑。不去计算 K，而是在一个可靠理论的证明里寻找“某个字符串的复杂度超过 L”的证明。<bookmark mark='f'/>同样的论证说明，一旦 L 超过某个取决于理论的常数，搜索必然失败。几乎每个字符串都是随机的，而超过某个固定的大小，没有理论能证明其中任何一个是随机的。

94b530fcb43c.en: In 1975 Chaitin packed the halting problem into a single number. <bookmark mark='a'/> Pick a program at random by tossing a coin for each bit, until the bits spell out a complete program. <bookmark mark='b'/> If no program is the beginning of another, these probabilities add up to at most one. <bookmark mark='c'/> Omega is the probability that the program you get eventually halts: one real number between zero and one. <bookmark mark='d'/> You can approach it from below. Run every program side by side, and each time one halts, add its probability. <bookmark mark='e'/> The sums climb toward Omega, but nothing ever tells you how close you are.
94b530fcb43c.zh: 1975年，Chaitin 把停机问题装进了一个数里。<bookmark mark='a'/>随机挑一个程序：每一位抛一次硬币，直到这些位拼出一个完整的程序。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果没有程序是另一个程序的开头，这些概率加起来至多为一。<bookmark mark='c'/>Omega 就是你得到的程序终究会停机的概率：零和一之间的一个实数。<bookmark mark='d'/>你可以从下方逼近它。把所有程序并排运行，每有一个停机，就加上它的概率。<bookmark mark='e'/>这些和朝着 Omega 攀升，但没有任何东西会告诉你离它有多近。

86a728763d87.en: We cannot compute Omega, but we can compute a small cousin. <bookmark mark='a'/> Draw five thousand random Turing machines with three states, each rule choosing at random what to write, which way to move, and whether to go to another state or halt. Run each with a growing budget of steps, and count the fraction that has halted. <bookmark mark='b'/> It climbs, quickly at first. By sixteen steps it reaches forty-five percent, and after two thousand steps it has not moved. <bookmark mark='c'/> The longest halting run we saw was eleven steps. <bookmark mark='d'/> Here we know the curve is finished, because of Part 1: the three-state busy beaver runs twenty-one steps, so any three-state machine still running after twenty-one never stops. <bookmark mark='e'/> For a universal machine no such bound exists. Knowing when the curve was finished would mean knowing the busy beaver at every size.
86a728763d87.zh: 我们算不出 Omega，但能算出一个小表亲。<bookmark mark='a'/>随机抽五千台三状态图灵机，每条规则随机决定写什么、往哪边移、转到另一个状态还是停机。给每台机器一个不断增长的步数预算，统计已停机的比例。<bookmark mark='b'/>它在攀升，起初很快。到十六步时达到百分之四十五，两千步之后再也没动过。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们见到的最长的停机运行是十一步。<bookmark mark='d'/>在这里我们知道曲线已经到头，靠的是第1部分：三状态的忙碌海狸运行二十一步，所以任何运行超过二十一步的三状态机器都永不停机。<bookmark mark='e'/>对一台通用机，这样的界不存在。知道曲线何时到头，就意味着知道每种大小的忙碌海狸。

45c39b6e23a9.en: Omega is a strange number. <bookmark mark='a'/> Cristian Calude, Michael Dinneen and Chi-Kou Shu computed the first sixty-four bits for one particular universal machine in 2002. For larger machines, nobody can. Here is why. <bookmark mark='b'/> Suppose you knew the first n bits. Run every program side by side, adding up the probabilities of those that halt, until the sum reaches those n bits. <bookmark mark='c'/> Any program of n bits or fewer that is still running then can never halt: if it did, its contribution would push the total past Omega. <bookmark mark='d'/> So a few thousand bits of Omega would settle Goldbach's conjecture, the Riemann hypothesis and the consistency of set theory, each the halting of one short program. <bookmark mark='e'/> It follows that Omega is random: its first n bits cannot be compressed by more than a constant. <bookmark mark='f'/> And by chapter ten, a sound theory can determine only finitely many of its bits. Robert Solovay found a universal machine for which set theory cannot determine even one.
45c39b6e23a9.zh: Omega 是一个奇怪的数。<bookmark mark='a'/>Cristian Calude、Michael Dinneen 和 Chi-Kou Shu 在2002年为一台特定的通用机算出了前六十四位。对更大的机器，没人能做到。原因如下。<bookmark mark='b'/>假设你知道前 n 位。把每个程序并排运行，把停机程序的概率加起来，直到总和达到这 n 位。<bookmark mark='c'/>这时任何不超过 n 位、仍在运行的程序都永远不会停机：如果它停了，它的贡献会把总和推过 Omega。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以 Omega 的几千位就能解决 Goldbach 猜想、黎曼猜想和集合论的一致性，每一个都是某个短程序的停机问题。<bookmark mark='e'/>由此可知 Omega 是随机的：它的前 n 位压缩不了超过一个常数。<bookmark mark='f'/>而由第10章，一个可靠的理论只能确定它的有限多位。Robert Solovay 找到了一台通用机，集合论连它的一位都确定不了。

3702be29081c.en: Three speeds of growth. <bookmark mark='a'/> Programs whose loops have bounds fixed before they start, what logicians call primitive recursion, can compute two to the n, towers of twos, and any fixed stack of such things. <bookmark mark='b'/> Part 11 met Wilhelm Ackermann's function and promised to say why it matters. It is computable and always finishes, yet it eventually outgrows every function that bounded loops can compute. A of four, four is already a tower of twos with sixty-five thousand five hundred and thirty-six in the top exponent. <bookmark mark='c'/> The reason is the diagonal argument once more. A language in which every program finishes has an interpreter that always finishes too, but the interpreter cannot be written in that language. <bookmark mark='d'/> If it could, so could d of x, the interpreter run on x with input x, plus one. Run d on its own code and you get d of d equals d of d plus one. That is the argument Part 14 pointed to, for why the typed lambda calculus cannot interpret itself. <bookmark mark='e'/> And the third column outgrows even Ackermann. Part 1 stated that the busy beaver outgrows every computable function. Now the proof.
3702be29081c.zh: 三种增长速度。<bookmark mark='a'/>循环界限在开始前就固定的程序，逻辑学家称之为原始递归，能计算二的 n 次方、二的塔，以及任何固定层数的这类东西。<bookmark mark='b'/>第11部分遇到过 Wilhelm Ackermann 的函数，并许诺说明它为什么重要。它可计算，总会结束，却终将超过有界循环能计算的每一个函数。A 四四已经是一座二的塔，最顶上的指数是六万五千五百三十六。<bookmark mark='c'/>原因又是对角线论证。一个每个程序都会结束的语言，有一个总会结束的解释器，但这个解释器不能用这个语言写出来。<bookmark mark='d'/>如果能，那么 d 也能：d of x 是解释器在 x 上以 x 为输入运行，再加一。把 d 运行在它自己的代码上，就得到 d of d 等于 d of d 加一。这就是第14部分提到过的论证，说明了为什么类型化 lambda 演算不能解释它自己。<bookmark mark='e'/>而第三列连 Ackermann 也超过了。第1部分说过忙碌海狸超过每一个可计算函数。现在给出证明。

af72688c607c.en: The proof is a machine built in three pieces. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take any computable function f, computed by a machine with c states. For each n, build a machine that first writes n on its tape, which takes n states; <bookmark mark='b'/> then computes f of two n, which takes c states; then counts that number down to zero, a few states more. <bookmark mark='c'/> It has n plus a constant states, and it halts after more than f of two n steps. <bookmark mark='d'/> So the busy beaver of n plus that constant is bigger than f of two n. <bookmark mark='e'/> Once n is larger than the constant, the busy beaver of two n is bigger still. The busy beaver passes f and stays ahead. <bookmark mark='f'/> No computable function can even bound it.
af72688c607c.zh: 证明是一台由三块拼成的机器。<bookmark mark='a'/>任取一个可计算函数 f，由一台有 c 个状态的机器计算。对每个 n，造一台机器，先把 n 写到纸带上，这要用 n 个状态；<bookmark mark='b'/>然后计算 f 的二 n，这要用 c 个状态；然后把这个数倒数到零，再多几个状态。<bookmark mark='c'/>它有 n 加一个常数个状态，停机前运行超过 f 的二 n 步。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以 n 加这个常数处的忙碌海狸大于 f 的二 n。<bookmark mark='e'/>一旦 n 大于这个常数，二 n 处的忙碌海狸就更大。忙碌海狸超过了 f，并且一直领先。<bookmark mark='f'/>没有可计算函数能给它设一个上界。

6cd6f11f4f70.en: Part 1 told how the five-state value was proved, and why six may be out of reach. Here is the larger map. <bookmark mark='a'/> Many open problems are the halting of a single small machine. A fifteen-state machine, from Tristan Stérin and Damien Woods in 2021, halts exactly if Erdős was wrong that every power of two beyond the eighth has a digit two in base three. A twenty-seven-state machine, posted online in 2015 and not yet checked carefully, halts if Goldbach's conjecture fails. Seven hundred and forty-four states encode the Riemann hypothesis. <bookmark mark='b'/> So knowing the busy beaver of twenty-seven would settle Goldbach, at least in principle: run the machine that long. <bookmark mark='c'/> And some machine of a few hundred states halts only if set theory is inconsistent, so by chapter eight, set theory cannot prove its busy-beaver value. Any sound theory pins down only finitely many values. <bookmark mark='d'/> Somewhere between six and four hundred and thirty-two, set theory's knowledge stops. Where, exactly, nobody knows.
6cd6f11f4f70.zh: 第1部分讲过五状态的值是怎样证明的，以及为什么六状态也许遥不可及。这里是更大的地图。<bookmark mark='a'/>许多未解问题就是某一台小机器的停机问题。Tristan Stérin 和 Damien Woods 在2021年给出的一台十五状态机器，停机恰好当 Erdős 错了：他认为第八次方以后的每个二的幂在三进制下都有一个数字二。一台二十七状态的机器，2015年发布在网上，尚未经过仔细核查，在 Goldbach 猜想不成立时停机。七百四十四个状态编码了黎曼猜想。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以知道二十七处的忙碌海狸，至少在原则上就能解决 Goldbach：把那台机器运行那么久。<bookmark mark='c'/>而某台几百个状态的机器只在集合论不一致时停机，所以由第8章，集合论无法证明它的忙碌海狸值。任何可靠的理论都只能确定有限多个值。<bookmark mark='d'/>在六和四百三十二之间的某处，集合论的知识停住了。究竟在哪里，没人知道。

3a04ffb679c2.zh: 第13章。可判定性在哪里终止。

f1df83271aa8.en: Not every mathematical theory is undecidable. Here is where the line falls. <bookmark mark='a'/> Mojżesz Presburger showed in 1929 that the truths about whole numbers with addition alone can be decided by a machine, though Michael Fischer and Michael Rabin proved it takes at least doubly exponential time. <bookmark mark='b'/> Alfred Tarski showed the same for the real numbers with addition, multiplication and order, and with them all of Euclid's geometry. <bookmark mark='c'/> Add multiplication to the whole numbers and decidability is lost, by chapter eight. <bookmark mark='d'/> Julia Robinson showed the rationals are no better, because the integers can be defined inside them. <bookmark mark='e'/> And if you allow only equations, with no for-all, over the rationals? Nobody knows. That is this part's frontier. <bookmark mark='f'/> The pattern: multiplication of whole numbers is what lets numbers encode a computation. The reals escape because no formula can pick the whole numbers out of them.
f1df83271aa8.zh: 并不是每个数学理论都不可判定。这里是分界线所在。<bookmark mark='a'/>Mojżesz Presburger 在1929年证明，只有加法的整数的真理可以由机器判定，不过 Michael Fischer 和 Michael Rabin 证明这至少需要双重指数时间。<bookmark mark='b'/>Alfred Tarski 对带加法、乘法和序的实数证明了同样的事，连同整个欧几里得几何。<bookmark mark='c'/>给整数加上乘法，可判定性就丢了，由第8章。<bookmark mark='d'/>Julia Robinson 证明有理数也好不到哪去，因为整数可以在其中定义出来。<bookmark mark='e'/>如果只允许方程，不允许“对所有”，在有理数上呢？没人知道。那是这一部分的前沿。<bookmark mark='f'/>规律是：整数的乘法让数能够编码计算。实数逃脱了，因为没有公式能从中挑出整数。

9dce3aaa5644.en: Undecidability also hides in pure algebra. <bookmark mark='a'/> Max Dehn asked in 1911: given a group by finitely many generators and relations, can you decide whether a word in the generators equals the identity? Pyotr Novikov in 1955 and William Boone in 1958 found groups where no algorithm can. <bookmark mark='b'/> Or take a handful of three-by-three integer matrices. Does some product of them, in some order, with repetition, give the zero matrix? Michael Paterson proved in 1970 that this is undecidable, by turning Post's dominoes into matrices. <bookmark mark='c'/> For two-by-two matrices nobody knows.
9dce3aaa5644.zh: 不可判定性也藏在纯代数里。<bookmark mark='a'/>Max Dehn 在1911年问：给定一个由有限多个生成元和关系定义的群，你能判定生成元组成的一个词是否等于单位元吗？Pyotr Novikov 在1955年、William Boone 在1958年找到了没有算法能做到的群。<bookmark mark='b'/>或者拿几个三乘三的整数矩阵。它们按某种顺序、允许重复的某个乘积，会得到零矩阵吗？Michael Paterson 在1970年证明这不可判定，办法是把 Post 的多米诺变成矩阵。<bookmark mark='c'/>对二乘二的矩阵，没人知道。

46b98eca21dd.en: John Conway invented the strangest programming language of all. <bookmark mark='a'/> A program is a list of fractions. Start with a number; repeatedly multiply it by the first fraction in the list that gives a whole number; stop when none does. <bookmark mark='b'/> This list, PRIMEGAME, starts from two. Watch only the powers of two. After nineteen steps, four, which is two squared. After sixty-nine, eight. Then thirty-two, a hundred and twenty-eight, two to the eleven. <bookmark mark='c'/> The exponents are exactly the primes, in order. Our run reached every prime up to a hundred and twenty-seven in under three million steps. <bookmark mark='d'/> Why does this work? The exponents of the primes in n act as registers, and each fraction is an instruction that decrements some registers and increments others. That is Part 1's counter machine, and it is universal. <bookmark mark='e'/> So whether a list of fractions ever stops is undecidable.
46b98eca21dd.zh: John Conway 发明了最奇怪的编程语言。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个程序是一串分数。从一个数开始；反复把它乘以列表中第一个能得到整数的分数；没有这样的分数时停下。<bookmark mark='b'/>这个列表叫 PRIMEGAME，从二开始。只看二的幂。十九步后，四，也就是二的平方。六十九步后，八。然后是三十二、一百二十八、二的十一次方。<bookmark mark='c'/>指数恰好是素数，按顺序。我们的运行在不到三百万步里得到了直到一百二十七的每个素数。<bookmark mark='d'/>为什么行得通？n 里各个素数的指数充当寄存器，每个分数是一条指令，减少某些寄存器、增加另一些。那就是第1部分的计数器机，它是通用的。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以一串分数是否终究会停下，是不可判定的。

a857debc15d1.en: The most famous problem on the boundary is a children's puzzle. <bookmark mark='a'/> Halve an even number; triple an odd one and add one. Does every start reach one? Twenty-seven takes a hundred and eleven steps and climbs past nine thousand on the way. <bookmark mark='b'/> Below a million the longest journey is from eight hundred and thirty-seven thousand, seven hundred and ninety-nine: five hundred and twenty-four steps. <bookmark mark='c'/> Every start below two to the sixty-eight has been checked. <bookmark mark='d'/> Conway proved in 1972 that rules of exactly this shape, where n modulo some number chooses a linear map, can encode any program, so the general question is undecidable. <bookmark mark='e'/> The Collatz rule itself may be one of those cases, true but unprovable, or merely very hard. Nobody knows which, and Part 1's Antihydra is its cousin.
a857debc15d1.zh: 边界上最著名的问题是一个儿童谜题。<bookmark mark='a'/>偶数减半；奇数乘三加一。每个起点都会到达一吗？二十七要一百一十一步，途中爬过九千。<bookmark mark='b'/>一百万以内，最长的旅程从八十三万七千七百九十九出发：五百二十四步。<bookmark mark='c'/>二的六十八次方以下的每个起点都已检查过。<bookmark mark='d'/>Conway 在1972年证明，恰好这种形状的规则，即用 n 除以某数的余数来选一个线性映射，可以编码任何程序，所以一般问题不可判定。<bookmark mark='e'/>Collatz 规则本身也许就是这样的情形之一，真但不可证，也许只是非常难。没人知道是哪一种，而第1部分的 Antihydra 是它的表亲。

4d3164f55337.en: Chapter fourteen. Undecidability in the wild.
4d3164f55337.zh: 第14章。野外的不可判定性。

fc4459292496.en: Programmers meet undecidability by accident. <bookmark mark='a'/> C++ templates were meant for generic containers. In 2003 Todd Veldhuizen showed they form a complete programming language running inside the compiler, which is why compilers stop at a fixed template depth. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2017 Radu Grigore proved that subtyping with Java generics is undecidable: no compiler can always tell whether one type fits another. TypeScript's type system can run any program too, and its checker gives up at a depth limit. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 2019 Alex Churchill, Stella Biderman and Austin Herrick built a Turing machine out of the cards of Magic: the Gathering, so deciding who wins a given position is undecidable. <bookmark mark='d'/> Stephen Dolan showed that the x86 move instruction, alone, is Turing complete. <bookmark mark='e'/> And Conway's Game of Life, which Part 1 met, runs Turing machines made of gliders, like this one, walking diagonally across the grid. <bookmark mark='f'/> The lesson: give any configuration language, type system or rule set enough power, and some question about it becomes undecidable. Good designs decide on purpose where to stop.
fc4459292496.zh: 程序员会意外地撞上不可判定性。<bookmark mark='a'/>C++ 模板本来是为泛型容器设计的。2003年，Todd Veldhuizen 证明它们构成了一门在编译器内部运行的完整编程语言，这就是为什么编译器会在一个固定的模板深度停下。<bookmark mark='b'/>2017年，Radu Grigore 证明了 Java 泛型的子类型判定不可判定：没有编译器总能判断一个类型是否适配另一个。TypeScript 的类型系统也能运行任何程序，它的检查器在一个深度上限处放弃。<bookmark mark='c'/>2019年，Alex Churchill、Stella Biderman 和 Austin Herrick 用《万智牌》的卡牌造出了一台图灵机，所以判定一个给定局面谁赢是不可判定的。<bookmark mark='d'/>Stephen Dolan 证明，x86 的 mov 指令单独就是图灵完备的。<bookmark mark='e'/>而第1部分见过的 Conway 生命游戏，能运行由滑翔机组成的图灵机，比如这一个，沿对角线走过网格。<bookmark mark='f'/>教训是：给任何配置语言、类型系统或规则集足够的能力，关于它的某个问题就会变得不可判定。好的设计会有意识地决定在哪里停下。

364c4d68ea89.en: Undecidability reaches physics too. <bookmark mark='a'/> Model a material as particles on a grid, each interacting only with its neighbours by the same local rule. <bookmark mark='b'/> Its spectral gap is the energy it takes to lift the system out of its lowest state, in the limit of a large grid. <bookmark mark='c'/> Whether there is a gap decides much of how the material behaves. <bookmark mark='d'/> In 2015 Toby Cubitt, David Pérez-García and Michael Wolf proved that, for two-dimensional lattices, whether a gap exists is undecidable. <bookmark mark='e'/> Their construction is this part in miniature: the ground state is built from Robinson's aperiodic tiles, each tile running a Turing machine, and whether the gap closes depends on whether the machine halts.
364c4d68ea89.zh: 不可判定性也延伸到了物理。<bookmark mark='a'/>把一种材料建模成网格上的粒子，每个粒子只按同一条局部规则与邻居相互作用。<bookmark mark='b'/>它的谱隙，是在网格很大的极限下，把系统抬离最低能态所需的能量。<bookmark mark='c'/>有没有谱隙，很大程度上决定了材料的行为。<bookmark mark='d'/>2015年，Toby Cubitt、David Pérez-García 和 Michael Wolf 证明，对二维晶格，谱隙是否存在是不可判定的。<bookmark mark='e'/>他们的构造就是这一部分的缩影：基态由 Robinson 的非周期砖构成，每块砖里运行一台图灵机，而谱隙是否闭合取决于这台机器是否停机。

3db37465040a.en: Chapter fifteen, the frontier. Hilbert's tenth problem over other rings.
3db37465040a.zh: 第15章，前沿。其他环上的希尔伯特第十问题。

2550a9a0690d.en: Hilbert asked about the integers. What about other number systems? <bookmark mark='a'/> The Gaussian integers, numbers of the form a plus b root two, and in general the ring of integers of any number field. Can a machine decide whether an equation with such coefficients has a solution in such numbers? <bookmark mark='b'/> In 1978 Jan Denef and Leonard Lipshitz proposed the strategy: show that the ordinary integers form a Diophantine set inside the bigger ring, and Matiyasevich's theorem carries over. <bookmark mark='c'/> That was done for many fields in the 1980s, and for all of them in 2010, but only by assuming an unproved conjecture about elliptic curves. <bookmark mark='d'/> In December 2024 Peter Koymans and Carlo Pagano proved it for every number field, with no assumption. <bookmark mark='e'/> The key was to find, for each field, elliptic curves whose rank does not grow in a certain quadratic extension, and they found them with additive combinatorics, the tools of the Green-Tao theorem on primes in progressions. <bookmark mark='f'/> Levent Alpöge, Manjul Bhargava, Wei Ho and Ari Shnidman reached the same result independently, by another route. <bookmark mark='g'/> Combined with earlier work, the problem is now undecidable over every infinite ring that is finitely generated over the integers.
2550a9a0690d.zh: Hilbert 问的是整数。其他数系呢？<bookmark mark='a'/>高斯整数，形如 a 加 b 根号二的数，一般地，任意数域的整数环。机器能判定一个系数取自这样的数、要求解也取自这样的数的方程是否有解吗？<bookmark mark='b'/>1978年，Jan Denef 和 Leonard Lipshitz 提出了策略：证明普通整数在更大的环里构成一个丢番图集，Matiyasevich 定理就能搬过去。<bookmark mark='c'/>1980年代对许多数域做到了，2010年对所有数域也做到了，但要假设一个关于椭圆曲线的未证猜想。<bookmark mark='d'/>2024年12月，Peter Koymans 和 Carlo Pagano 对每个数域都证明了它，不需任何假设。<bookmark mark='e'/>关键是为每个数域找到在某个二次扩张里秩不增长的椭圆曲线，而他们是用加性组合找到的，也就是 Green-Tao 关于等差数列中素数的定理所用的工具。<bookmark mark='f'/>Levent Alpöge、Manjul Bhargava、Wei Ho 和 Ari Shnidman 沿另一条路独立得到了同样的结果。<bookmark mark='g'/>结合早先的工作，这个问题现在在每一个整数上有限生成的无限环上都不可判定。

39c8bd4838e8.en: The rationals are different. <bookmark mark='a'/> Over the rationals, an equation like y squared equals x cubed minus two is a question about rational points on a curve, the subject of arithmetic geometry, and Fermat knew the point three, five. <bookmark mark='b'/> If the integers formed a Diophantine set inside the rationals, the problem would be undecidable, just as before. <bookmark mark='c'/> But Barry Mazur conjectured in 1992 that rational points are never scattered enough for that, and most experts believe him. <bookmark mark='d'/> With quantifiers, the integers can be defined: Bjorn Poonen in 2009, and Jochen Koenigsmann in 2016 with a single for-all. <bookmark mark='e'/> So the full theory of the rationals is undecidable, as chapter thirteen said, but the equations alone might still be decidable. That is one of the great open problems of logic and number theory. <bookmark mark='f'/> Even over the integers, whether you can decide equations in just two unknowns is unknown.
39c8bd4838e8.zh: 有理数不一样。<bookmark mark='a'/>在有理数上，像 y 的平方等于 x 的立方减二这样的方程，是一个关于曲线上有理点的问题，那是算术几何的课题，而费马就知道点三、五。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果整数在有理数里构成一个丢番图集，这个问题就会像以前一样不可判定。<bookmark mark='c'/>但 Barry Mazur 在1992年猜想，有理点永远不会散布得足以做到这一点，大多数专家相信他。<bookmark mark='d'/>借助量词，整数是可以定义的：2009年的 Bjorn Poonen，以及2016年用单个“对所有”的 Jochen Koenigsmann。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以有理数的完整理论不可判定，正如第13章所说，但单是方程也许仍然可判定。那是逻辑与数论的伟大未解问题之一。<bookmark mark='f'/>即使在整数上，只有两个未知数的方程能否判定，也是未知的。

9b65644f1b17.en: A recurring frontier question is how small an undecidable problem can be. <bookmark mark='a'/> For equations over the natural numbers, nine unknowns are enough, by Matiyasevich and James Jones. Over the integers, Sun Zhi-Wei brought it to eleven in 2021. With one unknown it is easy; with two, over the integers, nobody knows. <bookmark mark='b'/> Post's dominoes: five is enough, two is decidable, three and four are open. A Turing machine with two states and three symbols was shown universal, in a weak sense, by Alex Smith in 2007. The busy beaver leaves set theory somewhere below four hundred and thirty-two states, and matrix mortality waits at two by two. <bookmark mark='c'/> Every gap in the third column is a research problem about exactly where computation begins.
9b65644f1b17.zh: 一个反复出现的前沿问题是：一个不可判定的问题最小能有多小。<bookmark mark='a'/>对自然数上的方程，九个未知数就够了，出自 Matiyasevich 和 James Jones。在整数上，孙智伟在2021年把它降到十一个。一个未知数时很容易；两个未知数，在整数上，没人知道。<bookmark mark='b'/>Post 的多米诺：五张就够，两张可判定，三张和四张未解。一台两状态、三符号的图灵机，被 Alex Smith 在2007年证明在一种弱的意义下是通用的。忙碌海狸在四百三十二个状态以下的某处离开集合论，矩阵致死性则停在二乘二。<bookmark mark='c'/>第三列里的每一个空缺，都是一个关于计算究竟从哪里开始的研究问题。

f39ee02282a9.en: Five open problems from this part. <bookmark mark='a'/> Hilbert's tenth over the rationals. <bookmark mark='b'/> Post's problem for three or four dominoes. <bookmark mark='c'/> A natural problem of intermediate degree, which nobody has ever found. <bookmark mark='d'/> The exact point where set theory loses track of the busy beaver. <bookmark mark='e'/> And whether the Collatz conjecture, if true, can be proved from the ordinary axioms of arithmetic. <bookmark mark='f'/> This part's research problem takes the second, for three dominoes.
f39ee02282a9.zh: 这一部分的五个未解问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>有理数上的希尔伯特第十问题。<bookmark mark='b'/>三张或四张多米诺的 Post 问题。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个中间度的自然问题，从来没人找到过。<bookmark mark='d'/>集合论失去对忙碌海狸掌控的确切位置。<bookmark mark='e'/>以及 Collatz 猜想如果为真，能否从普通的算术公理证明。<bookmark mark='f'/>这一部分的研究问题取第二个，三张多米诺的情形。

ce85c41c3f15.en: What we built in this part. Decidable, recognizable and co-recognizable, and reductions that carry impossibility from one problem to the next. Rice's theorem, which forbids almost every question about what programs do. Programs that print their own source, in Python and in Pebble. Dominoes, tiles and Diophantine equations, each hiding a Turing machine, and the hat. Gödel's theorems, proved from halting; oracles and the arithmetic hierarchy; Kolmogorov complexity and Chaitin's Omega; and the busy beaver, where proof runs out.
ce85c41c3f15.zh: 这一部分我们造了什么。可判定、可识别与补可识别，以及把不可能性从一个问题带到下一个问题的归约。Rice 定理，它禁止了几乎所有关于程序行为的问题。打印自己源代码的程序，用 Python，也用 Pebble。多米诺、砖块和丢番图方程，每一个都藏着一台图灵机，还有帽子。从停机证明的 Gödel 定理；谕示与算术层级；Kolmogorov 复杂度与 Chaitin 的 Omega；以及忙碌海狸，在那里证明走到了尽头。

7817f9b9e1a1.en: Where this comes back. Part 26 proves the time hierarchy theorem with the same diagonal, and asks the question this part cannot answer: not whether, but how fast. Part 54 proves programs correct, and escapes Rice's theorem by approximating. Part 55 shows that safety in access control is undecidable, and builds Ken Thompson's trojan compiler on a quine. Part 57 turns Kolmogorov's idea into Occam's razor for learning, and Part 58 makes recursion a fixed point, the semantic cousin of Kleene's theorem.
7817f9b9e1a1.zh: 这些会在哪里再出现。第26部分用同样的对角线证明时间层级定理，并提出这一部分无法回答的问题：不是能不能，而是多快。第54部分证明程序正确，靠近似逃出Rice 定理。第55部分说明访问控制中的安全性不可判定，并在一个自打印程序上造出 Ken Thompson 的特洛伊编译器。第57部分把 Kolmogorov 的思想变成学习中的奥卡姆剃刀，第58部分把递归变成不动点，那是 Kleene 定理在语义学里的表亲。

048df58dbbaf.en: In practice. Every static analyzer is an approximation, trading false alarms against missed bugs, because of Rice. No malware scanner is perfect, so security relies on sandboxes and limits rather than prediction. Language designers keep configuration files, query languages and some type systems deliberately less than Turing complete, so their questions stay decidable. Compilers cap template and type-checking depth. And Dijkstra's remark, that testing can show the presence of bugs but never their absence, is the halting problem in disguise.
048df58dbbaf.zh: 在实践中。每个静态分析器都是一种近似，在误报和漏报之间权衡，因为 Rice。没有完美的恶意软件扫描器，所以安全依赖沙箱和限制，而不是预测。语言设计者有意让配置文件、查询语言和某些类型系统达不到图灵完备，好让关于它们的问题保持可判定。编译器给模板和类型检查的深度设上限。而 Dijkstra 的那句话，测试能显示 bug 的存在却永远不能显示它们不存在，就是改头换面的停机问题。

2f6ffd17523d.en: Six problems, with full solutions in the part's notes. Pause on any of them. The fifth is a build problem: a program in the Pebble language that prints its own source backwards. The last, marked with a star, is a research problem: its answer is not known, and the notes say where to start.
2f6ffd17523d.zh: 六道习题，完整解答在这一部分的笔记里。随时暂停。第五道是动手题：一个用 Pebble 语言写的、把自己的源代码倒着打印出来的程序。最后一道标着星号，是研究问题：它的答案未知，笔记里说明了从哪里入手。

b896d30f79d3.en: Next time: this part asked what can be computed at all. Part 26 asks what can be computed quickly. In 1956 Gödel wrote to John von Neumann asking whether finding a proof could be as easy as checking one. Cook and Levin turned that letter into a single problem, Karp found it inside twenty-one others, and fifty years of attacks have failed. Part 26, P versus NP.
b896d30f79d3.zh: 下一次：这一部分问的是究竟什么能被计算。第26部分问什么能被快速计算。1956年，Gödel 写信给 John von Neumann，问找到一个证明是否可能和检查一个证明一样容易。Cook 和 Levin 把那封信变成了一个问题，Karp 在另外二十一个问题里找到了它，而五十年的进攻都失败了。第26部分，P 与 NP。

9bd24692775d.en: The books and papers this part follows are on screen and in the notes. Thank you for watching.
9bd24692775d.zh: 这一部分所依据的书和论文都在屏幕上和笔记里。感谢观看。
